GeM yields the lowest FP rate (3%) — only 1 false retrieval across 5 sequences. NetVLAD has the highest FP burden (13 pairs, 30% FP rate). XFeat-1D and XFeat-2D strike a balance with moderate recall and low FP rates.

Reprojection Error Analysis

Median Reproj. Error vs RANSAC Budget — by Retrieval Method
Median Reproj. Error by Retrieval Method (budget=10k)
Reprojection Error vs RANSAC Budget — per Feature Method
Inlier Ratio vs Reprojection Error (budget=10k)
Key finding: At budget=10,000, TP pairs achieve median reprojection errors of 0.43–0.45 px across all retrieval methods. FP pairs from GeM have higher reproj. error (0.52 px) while FP from XFeat-1D/2D are similar to TPs — suggesting RANSAC geometrically fits FPs but produces large angular errors (see Rotation section).

Rotation Error Analysis

Rotation Error vs RANSAC Budget — by Retrieval Method
Rotation Error by Retrieval Method (budget=10k)
Rotation Error vs RANSAC Budget — per Feature Method
Rotation Error Convergence — All Methods (TP vs FP)
Key finding: Rotation error is the clearest TP/FP discriminator. TPs consistently cluster at ≈18–30° (TP = small relative rotation), while FPs range from 65° (GeM) to 107° (XFeat-1D/2D). All 12 feature methods show the same sharp TP cluster — rotation error is method-agnostic and driven entirely by whether the retrieved pair is a true loop closure.

Translation Direction Error Analysis

Translation Direction Error vs RANSAC Budget — by Retrieval Method
Translation Direction Error by Retrieval Method (budget=10k)
Translation Direction Error vs RANSAC Budget — per Feature Method
Key finding: Translation direction error is less discriminative than rotation. TPs sit at 35–48° and FPs at 29–70° — significant overlap exists. This is expected: the essential matrix allows a 4-fold sign ambiguity in translation, and FPs that happen to share similar scene structure can produce geometrically consistent (but spurious) translation estimates.
